title: Panoramic dental X-ray (OPG)
what: One picture that shows all your teeth, jaws, and roots. The machine moves around your head. The radiation dose is small.
why: Before treatment, extraction, or implants, with braces, for pain, or to find hidden problems.
duration: usually 5 minutes, the picture itself about 15 seconds
tell_doctor: If you are pregnant or could be pregnant
If you have removable dentures or plates

prepare.title: Preparation
prepare.text: No special prep needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off earrings, chains, glasses, face and mouth piercings, and hair clips. Removable dentures come out too.

steps: You put on a protective apron
You stand in the machine with your chin on the rest
You bite on a disposable mouthpiece
Close your lips and press your tongue to the roof of your mouth
The machine slowly moves around your head. Do not move
feel: The machine hums quietly and moves close to your face
after: You can go back to your day straight away
The image is usually ready right away. You get it on a disc, by email, or in an app

faq.q: Is a panoramic dental X-ray harmful?
faq.a: The dose is very small, less than a chest screening X-ray. The benefit for your treatment is much greater.

faq.q: How is an OPG different from a dental CT scan?
faq.a: An OPG is a flat picture of all your teeth. A CT gives a 3D view. It is done, for example, before implants.
